flags.message: All three predictions were written between 19:10Z and 19:25Z on 2026-11-19, the day the application was referred and denied. outcome.json records only the date, so the record cannot show whether the order had issued before the predictions ran. codex-baseline fetched the live supremecourt.gov docket JSON for the linked petition No. 26-6187 at 19:12Z that day; the logged commands print only the Nov 18 petition-filing entry (one query's filter is truncated in the log) and its prose shows no knowledge of the result, so I graded leakage not_applicable for all three. A maintainer with the order's timestamp could confirm the cell was genuinely open.

All three predictions were created on the resolution date (2026-11-19, about 14:35-14:57Z), and outcome.json's resolved_at carries a date only. I graded leakage as not applicable on the strength of the withdrawal letter's docket filename stamp (2026-11-19 15:55) being later than the predictions, plus the two candidates that checked the live docket reporting it as still pending. A resolution timestamp in the outcome would make this same-day ordering checkable directly.

gemini-baseline's reasoning.md attributes facts and pinpoint citations to documents that do not contain them: a December 2013 clemency interview, a Florida Supreme Court holding that the clemency claim was untimely and procedurally barred under Fla. R. Crim. P. 3.851(d) ('slip op. at 10-11 & n.6', 'application-response.txt at 5-6'), and a single-claim application. The staged application and response say none of this, and a CourtListener check of the decision below (opinion 11528932) found no 'interview' or 'untimely' and a merits rejection of the clemency claim. I lowered reasoning_quality to 0.45 on that basis; a grader who did not check the decision below would likely grade it higher, so expect panel disagreement on this cell. Prediction, correct and brier_score are unaffected.

In record/documents/petition.txt (truncated: true, 216 PDF pages), the appendix-trimming heuristic cut 42,173 characters from PDF pages 21-53 as an 'appendix item' while retaining Appendices A-E in full; per the Petition's Table of Contents, PDF pages 21-53 are actually pages 7-36 of the Petition's own Reasons for Granting the Writ (likely triggered by 'Appendix A' appearing earlier in the front-matter Table of Appendices). Impact on this cell was minimal because questions-presented.txt, the Petition's full Table of Contents and Table of Authorities, Appendix H (summary-judgment brief), and decision-below.txt were all intact.

The first truncation marker in petition.txt labels PDF pages 21–53 as an appendix item. The cut begins on printed page 7 and removes most of the Reasons for Granting the Writ, including the city's discussion of competing decisions. I recovered the argument from the filed PDF linked in documents.json and completed the forecast.

codex-baseline, gemini-baseline, and claude-baseline are labeled forward, but their run 20261114T033825Z, November 14 retrieval timestamps, and prediction.created_at values follow outcome.resolved_at = 2026-11-13. An already-decided application was therefore provisioned forward with a truncated November 12 arrival snapshot. Check mode/timing classification before treating these cells as prospective performance. Leakage was assessed separately from that designation; quantitative scores are unchanged.

gemini-baseline made unrestricted own-caption CourtListener searches after the recorded November 13 resolution (calls 27, 30, and 59 in its November 14 log). Under the contract query-based rule, retrieved_outcome_material is true and influence possible, so leakage_suspected is true. All rows are outcome_only: the log does not expose returned content or prove that the Supreme Court denial was seen. The disclosed November 9 district-court ruling is earlier legitimate context, not evidence of this application outcome. This is a possible-influence assessment, not a finding of admitted knowledge.

gemini-baseline's reasoning repeatedly asserts eleven cert-stage amicus briefs, initial response waivers, and an August 13, 2026 call for response, and uses those as positive grant signals. The staged docket shows three amicus briefs, response extensions, and no response waivers or call for response; the candidate's frozen context has amicus_briefs=null despite the prose quoting it as 11. Its appendix-completeness assertion also conflicts with the staged cut notes. These discrepancies reduce reasoning_quality. The original predictor snapshot and tool-result bodies are not staged, so their origin cannot be determined; no provisioning failure or outcome leakage is inferred.

gemini-baseline describes a September 29/October 19 distribution sequence, October 15 rescheduling and an October 30 conference, whereas the staged docket records July 22/October 28 distributions for September 28/November 13 with an August 14 response request. It also states initial registration in 1982 and Georgia cert denial March 3; the petition says 1985 and March 31. Its claimed 5–4 Georgia denial is unsubstantiated in the staged text. These discrepancies affect the rationale and forecast grades. All gemini-baseline retrieval results are outcome_only, and its original snapshot is not staged, so the origin of the conflicting account cannot be determined. No outcome leakage is inferred.

The docket records petitioner replies on August 31 and October 20, 2026, but the document manifest and cert-reply.txt provide only the August 31 reply to Irigoyen. codex-baseline and gemini-baseline recognize the missing later reply. Grading was completed from the available record without inferring its contents; the omission itself was not penalized.

The November 16 snapshot dates the petition filing April 15, 2026, but the petition cover is dated May 20, 2026 and its attachment URL carries a May 20 timestamp. The snapshot separately shows an April 16 order extending the filing deadline to May 20. The documents manifest repeats April 15 as entry_date. This appears to be a filing-date metadata inconsistency; no input was altered and it does not change these evaluations.

The brief in opposition entry (Oct 30 2026) is marked VIDED and is a consolidated response to Nos. 26-141 and 26-142, but context.vide_links is empty and no record/related/ was staged; the docket's Links field names only application 26A528. I read the companion's row through `fedcourts query --docket-number 26-141` instead. Also no decision-below.txt was staged (lower-court-docket.txt says CourtListener holds no opinion on the judgment date; the opinion issued Aug. 8, 2025, after the June 18, 2025 order).

Forward cell ran after its event resolved: outcome.json resolved_at is 2026-11-13 (application denied by Justice Sotomayor), while all three candidates' predictions (run 20261114T033825Z) were created 2026-11-14 on a 2026-11-12 snapshot holding only the submission entry. I found no logged call or prose in any candidate showing this application's disposition, so leakage is graded not_applicable / not suspected for codex-baseline, claude-baseline and gemini-baseline. Two limits on that finding: gemini-baseline's log is entirely outcome_only, and claude-baseline's generic recent-denials corpus query is visible only as a digest. A maintainer should decide whether these cells count as forward-stratum predictions.

gemini-baseline's reasoning.md presents as a direct quotation from Pet. 27 a concession that petitioner 'did not challenge the fundamental-rights prong of the shocks-the-conscience standard below'. The staged petition.txt contains no such sentence; page 27 states that the issue 'was pressed and passed upon at every stage'. The quoted concession supports one of the four stated downward adjustments and recurs in predicted_reasoning.md. It lowered reasoning_quality for that candidate; correct and brier_score are unaffected.

gemini-baseline's reasoning.md and predicted_reasoning.md describe a record that does not match the provisioned one: an interlocutory Fulton County discovery dispute with a Texas plaintiff, a 1989 registration, Mayer Brown as counsel, trial-court orders quoted at Pet. App. 3a-6a, and a Georgia Supreme Court denial on Mar. 3, 2026. The staged petition and docket show a $10.86M default judgment, a reasoned Georgia Court of Appeals opinion (June 23, 2025), a 1985 registration, Greenberg Traurig as counsel of record, and a March 31, 2026 denial. Its statpack figures (363/7,940 baseline) also match neither the committed pack nor the build in force at its run. Its transcript shows it opened the same petition.txt path, so this looks like the candidate's error, not a provisioning mix-up, but a maintainer may want to confirm. The disposition and Brier are unaffected; I graded reasoning_quality 0.2 on it.

gemini-baseline's reasoning.md and predicted_reasoning.md recite docket facts the staged record contradicts (brief in opposition Sep 2 and reply Sep 16; distribution Sep 29 for an Oct 16 conference, an Oct 15 reschedule, redistribution for Oct 30; a 5-4 Georgia Supreme Court denial on Mar 3, 2026). The docket shows distributions Jul 22 for 9/28 and Oct 28 for 11/13, the opposition Oct 14, the reply Oct 28, and a Mar 31, 2026 state order with all participating Justices concurring. The other two candidates, reading the same-named snapshot, report the docket correctly, so this looks like the candidate's error and not a provisioning fault; it is reflected in reasoning_quality and the forecast grade. Scores are unaffected.
